article_title: Teaching resources for the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education (EurOP2E)—a nominal group technique study
citation: Bakkum, M. J. et al. (2022). Teaching resources for the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education (EurOP2E)—a nominal group technique study. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-022-00141-y
title: EurOP²E — the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education
description: EurOP²E is a platform that "seeks to improve and harmonize European clinical pharmacology and therapeutics (CPT) education by facilitating international collaboration and sharing problem-based, online, open educational resources." It was set up to address the EACPT Education Working Group's recommendation 6, that schools utilize more online learning resources and share them nationally and internationally. Depending on the theme, its function will vary from supporting international communication and collaboration to providing teach-the-teacher materials and initiating collaborative production of ready-to-use teaching materials.
requirements: Open (free to re-use, adapt, and redistribute) distribution of resources
Teacher participation and collaboration across countries
constraints: Must be dynamic as educators' resource needs change with growing collaboration
Local/national differences in electronic prescribing systems must be accounted for when making such resources available for international use
target_learners: Medical and pharmacy students in European CPT education
target_learning_goals: Clinical pharmacology and therapeutics knowledge, skills and attitudes
examples: Participants proposed and ranked 35 teaching materials across four online meetings to inform what the platform should host
key_sources: Bakkum, M. J. et al. (2022). Teaching resources for the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education (EurOP2E)—a nominal group technique study. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-022-00141-y

article_title: An Approach to Integration: The Integration of Language and Content to Promote L2 Learner Autonomy at the College Level (Un Acercamiento a la Integración: El Aprendizaje Integrado de Lengua y Contenidos para Promover la Autonomía del Estudiante de Lengua Extranjera en la Universidad)
citation: Oliva Parera, P. M., & Núñez Delgado, M. P. (2015). An Approach to Integration: The Integration of Language and Content to promote L2 Learner Autonomy at the College Level. Gist Education and Learning Research Journal, 10, 92-112. https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN/1692-5777
title: European Language Portfolio (PEL) adapted for the American graduate university context
description: The European Portfolio for Languages, developed by the Language Policy Division of the Council of Europe, contains three distinctive elements: the "language passport" identifying the learner's skills, the "language biography" described as the axis of the portfolio where students reflect upon and evaluate their progress, and the dossier for storing information or skills. This research adapted the portfolio for use in a graduate university context at an American university, aiming to broaden the research base of the PEL regarding portfolios' role in encouraging student autonomy.
requirements: Teachers must consider what students say when analyzing their own work, since metacognition relates to students' control of learning situations
Portfolio sections including assessment needs, linguistic bibliography, and long- and short-term learning goals
constraints: The original PEL was developed in conjunction with the CEFR for the European community; this study adapted it to the American graduate context
target_learners: postgraduate university students learning a foreign language
examples: Students submitted portfolios at the end of the semester; experimental-group extracts show goals tied to MBA, environmental studies, and career language needs
key_sources: Oliva Parera, P. M., & Núñez Delgado, M. P. (2015). An Approach to Integration: The Integration of Language and Content to promote L2 Learner Autonomy at the College Level. Gist Education and Learning Research Journal, 10, 92-112. https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN/1692-5777

article_title: The Feasibility and Quality of the European Prescribing Exam: An International Multicenter Pilot Study Among 3109 Medical Students From 16 Medical Schools.
citation: Donker, E. M., Piët, J. D., Brinkman, D. J., Richir, M. C., Papaioannidou, P., Likic, R., Sanz, E. J., Christiaens, T., Costa, J. N., De Ponti, F., Böttiger, Y., Kramers, C., van Agtmael, M. A., & Tichelaar, J. (2026). The Feasibility and Quality of the European Prescribing Exam: An International Multicenter Pilot Study Among 3109 Medical Students From 16 Medical Schools. Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics. https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70063
title: European Prescribing Exam
description: A free-of-charge, standardized, cross-border online examination on safe prescribing developed through the Erasmus+ project EuroPE+ by nine medical schools, the EACPT, and the NVKFB. Each exam comprises "a knowledge part, containing 24 unique (case-based) multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and 12 unique multiple-answer medication review questions (MAQs), and a skills part containing 11 unique questions" on prescribing for clinical case scenarios. It is implemented as a formative examination, conducted in English, and covers eight main drug topics.
requirements: An assessment blueprint covering the first three levels of Miller's pyramid
Peer review of all questions by senior clinical pharmacologists and other medical specialists
constraints: Administered in English due to over 20 European languages
Students may use guidelines and formularies for the skills part but not for the knowledge part
target_learners: Fifth- and sixth- (final-) year medical students
target_learning_goals: Safe and effective prescribing knowledge and skills
examples: Administered to 3109 students from 16 medical schools in 11 European countries between October 2020 and August 2023
key_sources: Donker, E. M., Piët, J. D., Brinkman, D. J., Richir, M. C., Papaioannidou, P., Likic, R., Sanz, E. J., Christiaens, T., Costa, J. N., De Ponti, F., Böttiger, Y., Kramers, C., van Agtmael, M. A., & Tichelaar, J. (2026). article_title: Performance of single-agent and multi-agent language models in Spanish language medical competency exams.
citation: Altermatt Fernando R., Neyem Andres, Sumonte Nicolas, Mendoza Marcelo, Villagran Ignacio, Lacassie Hector J. (2025). Performance of single-agent and multi-agent language models in Spanish language medical competency exams. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07250-3
title: Curated EUNACOM question dataset of 1,062 Spanish-language medical licensure items
description: The study curated a dataset of "1,062 publicly available and previously administered EUNACOM questions", preprocessed with orthographic standardization and exclusion of image-based or multimodal content. Answer choices were randomized per run to minimize ordering biases, and each item carried a predefined correct answer used as an automated evaluation key. The dataset served as the benchmark for comparing ten prompting and multi-agent strategies on GPT-4o.
requirements: Questions must be multiple-choice with predefined correct answers to support fully automated scoring
constraints: Image-based and multimodal content was excluded, so results do not cover multimodal exam items
target_learners: medical trainees and physicians preparing for the Chilean EUNACOM licensure exam
target_learning_goals: specialized medical knowledge assessment across 21 medical specialties in Spanish
examples: GPT-4o was evaluated on the dataset under ten strategies, each tested twice at three temperature settings
key_sources: Altermatt Fernando R., Neyem Andres, Sumonte Nicolas, Mendoza Marcelo, Villagran Ignacio, Lacassie Hector J. (2025). Performance of single-agent and multi-agent language models in Spanish language medical competency exams. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07250-3

article_title: Using simulation to teach nursing students how to deal with a euthanasia request.
citation: Demedts, D., Magerman, J., Goossens, E., Tricas-Sauras, S., Bilsen, J., De Smet, S., & Fobelets, M. (2024). Using simulation to teach nursing students how to deal with a euthanasia request. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0299049
title: Euthanasia simulation module for nursing students: online learning module, good-practice video, role-play scenarios, and DML debriefing
description: A simulation module developed to prepare nursing students for dealing with a euthanasia request. In the authors' words, "three key components were incorporated: a preparatory phase consisting of an online PowerPoint, a good-practice video, and a simulation scenario; a simulation role-play; and a debriefing session." The module's content was validated by four Belgian end-of-life care experts, and it was completed by 17 final-year nursing students from two University Colleges in Flanders, Belgium.
requirements: Students complete a preparatory online learning module covering conversation techniques and the legal framework before the simulation session
Content validated by domain experts in end-of-life care
constraints: Focused on the first phase of the euthanasia process, initial care and accompaniment, not the later phases
Conclusions apply only to nursing students, not other healthcare students
examples: Three scenarios were enacted per session: one around cancer, one around polypathology, and one around unbearable mental suffering euthanasia
key_sources: Demedts, D., Magerman, J., Goossens, E., Tricas-Sauras, S., Bilsen, J., De Smet, S., & Fobelets, M. (2024). Using simulation to teach nursing students how to deal with a euthanasia request. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0299049
